name: Galaxy J5 (2015)
summary: ztOS on the Samsung Galaxy J5 (2015), the first port made with ztConflo: Arch Linux ARM with ztMETRO on postmarketOS's mainline msm8916 kernel (Linux 6.12), booted by lk2nd from the userdata partition. Snapdragon 410 with the Adreno 306 on Mesa's freedreno, so the whole UI runs on the GPU. The home key and the recents and back touch keys work as Windows Phone's hardware buttons, with haptics, so there is no on-screen nav bar. Wi-Fi, battery, vibration, torch and the speaker work; calls and the cameras are not done yet.
photo_caption: ztMETRO's Start on the Galaxy J5

install.markdown:
> **This erases the phone's user data.** ztOS is written to the userdata partition and lk2nd to BOOT. The modem, EFS (IMEI) and Samsung's bootloader are not touched. To go back, flash Samsung's stock firmware with Odin and factory-reset.
>
> **Tested on the SM-J500N0** (Snapdragon 410). Other Snapdragon J5 2015 models (J500F, J500FN, J500H is not Snapdragon) should work but are untested.

## What you need

- A Linux computer (x86-64) with **15 GB free** and an internet connection
- A micro-USB **data** cable (some only charge)
- The phone charged above **50%**
- About **1 hour**, mostly waiting

## 1. Install the tools on your computer

Arch Linux:

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed git python android-tools heimdall dtc e2fsprogs \
    arch-install-scripts qemu-user-static qemu-user-static-binfmt zstd cpio
```

## 2. Get ztConflo, the device registry and ztOS

```sh
mkdir -p ~/ztos && cd ~/ztos
git clone https://github.com/Zerone-Laboratories/ztconflo.git
git clone https://github.com/Zerone-Laboratories/ztos-devices.git
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Zerone-Laboratories/ztOS.git
```

## 3. Put TWRP on the phone

1. Download TWRP for the J5 (`twrp-3.7.0_9-0-j5lte.img.tar`) from https://twrp.me/samsung/samsunggalaxyj52015.html and unpack it:

```sh
cd ~/ztos
tar xf ~/Downloads/twrp-3.7.0_9-0-j5lte.img.tar
```

2. Turn the phone off. Hold **Volume Down + Home + Power** until the warning screen shows, then press **Volume Up**: the phone is in Download mode.
3. Connect it and flash TWRP:

```sh
heimdall flash --RECOVERY recovery.img --no-reboot
```

4. Hold **Power + Volume Down + Home** until the screen goes black, then at once switch to **Volume Up + Home + Power** and hold until TWRP shows. If Android starts instead, it replaces TWRP: do this step again.

## 4. Build ztOS for the J5

```sh
cd ~/ztos/ztconflo
python -m ztconflo build samsung-j5 --registry ../ztos-devices --ztos-src ../ztOS
```

It asks for your password once (`sudo`) and ends with the files in `out/samsung-j5/`. It takes about 30 to 60 minutes.

## 5. Flash it

With the phone in TWRP and connected:

```sh
adb devices
```

The phone must be listed as `recovery`. Then:

```sh
python -m ztconflo flash samsung-j5 --registry ../ztos-devices
```

It shows the partitions it will overwrite and asks you to type `samsung-j5`. It writes lk2nd to BOOT and ztOS to userdata, reads each one back, and reboots.

## 6. First boot

The first boot takes about a minute. The login is user `alarm`, password `alarm`. Over USB the phone is at `172.16.42.1`:

```sh
ssh alarm@172.16.42.1
```

Change the password with `passwd`.

features.notes: lk2nd on BOOT, ztOS from userdata through extlinux
Start; wakes the screen like the power key
TC360 read by ztos-touchkeyd; recents opens Hyperscan; no on-screen nav bar
SM5703 motor; haptics on the touch keys
The modem firmware loads; not tried with a SIM yet
The J5 has no light sensor
60 fps on Start and in the apps
Pages work; scrolling runs at about 40-45 fps on the Adreno 306

notes.title: Built with ztConflo
notes.text: The J5 has no hand-made device layer: ztConflo builds it from postmarketOS's port and the entry in ztos-devices, which adds the J5's battery, vibration, touch keys and modem memory fixes.

notes.title: Scrolling in Superscan
notes.text: Web pages scroll at about 40-45 fps: WebKit's composition takes 8-12 ms of the Adreno 306 a frame. ztWebKitv1, a WebKit tuned for these GPUs, is being worked on.
